text: Did A use the eraser to remove something from the sheet, thereby revealing the message?
Did A use the eraser as a tool to press or emboss the message into the paper, rather than mark it with ink or graphite?
Did A use the eraser itself to make visible marks on the paper, for example by transferring graphite or pigment from it?
Did A use the eraser together with a separate writing implement, such as a pencil, to write the message?
Did A leave the eraser on the paper so that text or a symbol already printed on the eraser served as the message?
Did A use the eraser to cause a change in the paper itself that encoded the message, without making visible marks?
Did the message become visible or readable on the sheet only after A had finished using the eraser?
Did A use the eraser to apply a substance to the paper that was initially invisible, with the message appearing after the paper was heated?
Did rubbing the eraser on the sheet make the message appear through friction or heat, as on heat-sensitive paper?
Did A use the eraser to trigger a chemical reaction that made the message appear on the paper?
Did A use the eraser to operate or trigger another device that produced the message on the paper?
Did the eraser help create a shadow or other optical effect that made a message appear on the paper, rather than writing or marking the paper itself?
Did using the eraser cause writing on a separate surface beneath or behind the sheet to transfer onto the sheet?
Did A use the eraser to abrade, tear, or perforate the paper so that the resulting holes or damage formed the message?
Did A use the eraser as a mask or stencil while applying some other substance to the paper, so that the substance formed the message?
Did A use the eraser to fold or shape the sheet so that its form, rather than marks on it, conveyed the message?
Did A make eraser crumbs or dust and arrange them on the sheet to form the message?
Did A use the eraser on something other than the sheet, and did that action indirectly cause a message to appear on the sheet?
Did A’s use of the eraser prompt another person to write or otherwise put the message on the sheet?
Did using the eraser remove or alter something on another surface, thereby uncovering or releasing a message that was already present on the sheet?
Did A’s action with the eraser cause an animal or an automatic physical process to put the message on the paper?
Did A use the eraser on another object to change its position or shape, causing the sheet to move or change and thereby revealing the message?
After using the eraser on something else, did A personally write the message on the sheet using a separate writing implement?
Did A use the eraser on a pencil or other writing implement to prepare it for writing the message on the sheet?
Did A rub the eraser against the pencil’s graphite tip to clean it before writing the message?
Did A use the eraser to remove or clear something from the pencil’s mechanism, such as a jam, so the pencil could write?
Did A use the eraser to sharpen the pencil’s graphite tip, or otherwise reshape the tip so it could write?
Was the writing implement an erasable pen, and did A use the eraser to remove something from it so it could write?
Was the writing implement an erasable pen?
Was the writing implement a pencil, rather than another kind of writing tool?
Did A use the eraser to remove a covering or obstruction from the pencil’s graphite, other than sharpening or reshaping its tip?
Did A use the eraser on the pencil’s non-writing end, rather than on its graphite tip or mechanism?
Did A rub the eraser on the pencil’s non-writing end to remove material and expose its graphite core for writing?
Was the pencil a mechanical pencil?
Did A press the eraser at the back of the mechanical pencil to advance its graphite lead before writing?
Did A remove the eraser or its cap from the back of the mechanical pencil to access its lead reservoir, allowing the pencil to be loaded with lead before writing?
Was the pencil out of lead, so A removed the eraser/cap to load lead into it before writing the message?

A wanted to write a message with a mechanical pencil, but it had run out of lead. The eraser was attached to the pencil’s back and covered the lead reservoir. A removed the eraser to access the reservoir, loaded lead into the pencil, and then used it to write on the previously blank sheet.
